newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-TAILENDERS CARRY INDIA TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAILENDERS CARRY INDIA TO VICTORY.

text.p: A half century
partnership by ninth-wicket pair Javagal Srinath and Anil Kumble
carried India to an exciting two-wicket victory over Australia
in the Titan Cup triangular tournament on Monday.
Srinath, who made 30 from 23 balls, and Kumble, 16 not out,
put on 52 off 40 deliveries to turn the tables on the
Australians.
Chasing 215 for seven, built around Mark Taylor's maiden
international one-day century, India had appeared in dire
straits at 164 for eight.
They eventually scrambled home with seven balls left.
Sachin Tendulkar had hauled his side out of an earlier
crisis -- they had stumbled to 47 for four -- with an
accomplished 88 off 111 balls with nine fours.
He took a leaf out of book of his opposite number Taylor,
who had grafted his way to 105 from 144 deliveries on a slow
pitch.
The Australian captain's previous one-day best was 97
against New Zealand in Auckland last year.
India's innings was interrupted for 20 minutes by spectators
who began hurling plastic water bottles on to the playing area
in protest over Mohammed Azharuddin's dismissal.
He was given out leg before by Indian umpire S.K. Bansal.
The bottle-throwing stopped only when Azharuddin pleaded
with the fans to behave.
